summary: Verified auto-reload on document delete (iteration 21). Backend: Cache-Control: no-store header is correctly applied by the no_store_api middleware to all tested /api endpoints — /api/health, /api/courses, /api/documents, /api/auth/me (5/5 pytests PASS in test_no_store_cache.py). Frontend desktop (1280x800) and mobile (390x844) delete flows PASS end-to-end: logged in via UI (test@copythat.app / 246810), created a test course + 2 docs, opened one doc, tapped doc-delete, accepted window.confirm, and verified that (a) the list of docs on /archive immediately drops from 2 → 1 WITHOUT a reload, (b) the sidebar course count also decreases (2 → 1 observed on desktop), (c) search hits for the deleted title also disappear immediately after delete+return (desktop), and (d) deep-link delete (opening /doc/<id> directly without history, then deleting) correctly lands on /archive with the deleted doc no longer in the list (mobile). documentDeleted(id) + onDocumentDeleted listener in archive.tsx and the cache:'no-store' fetch option in api.ts both behave as intended.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py no_store_api middleware (L843-849) correctly checks 'cache-control' not in response.headers before setting no-store, so export/filedownload responses with their own cache headers are preserved.
archive.tsx onDocumentDeleted listener (L64-72) updates docs, hits AND reloads loadCourses() for counts — correct and complete.

doc/[id].tsx deleteDoc (L126-148) treats 404 as success (idempotent double-tap), sets mounted.current=false to stop polling, calls documentDeleted(id) BEFORE navigation, and falls back to router.replace('/archive') when canGoBack() is false (deep-link case) — all correct.
api.ts api() uses cache:'no-store' on every fetch (L68) — correct iOS/Safari fix.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (desktop + mobile delete, search-delete, deep-link delete all PASS)

seed_data_creation: Created test courses TEST_Del_desktop_* and TEST_Del_mobile_* with 2 docs each via UI; all test data was removed through the UI delete-course trash button and a final API cleanup sweep (0 courses remaining under test user).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login via UI flow on /login (testIDs: login-email, login-send-code, login-code with 246810, login-verify). AsyncStorage on web uses IndexedDB, NOT localStorage. For mobile viewport (<900px wide), after creating a course from the sidebar screen you must tap the course row to switch to the doc-list screen before new-doc-input is rendered. For deep-link delete tests use page.goto('/doc/<id>') directly — doc/[id].tsx correctly uses router.replace('/archive') when there's no history.
rca_of_issue: Not a bug this iteration — this was fix verification. The reported user issue (deleted docs still shown until app restart) was caused by iOS/browser caching GET /api/documents (and no in-app event when a doc was deleted from the doc screen). Fix verified: (1) backend no_store_api middleware adds Cache-Control: no-store to /api/* responses; (2) frontend api.ts fetch uses cache:'no-store'; (3) doc/[id].tsx calls documentDeleted(id) after a successful delete and archive.tsx subscribes via onDocumentDeleted to drop the doc from docs/hits and reload course counts immediately — plus useFocusEffect still reloads on return. All three layers were observed working together in both desktop and mobile viewports.
